data.gender_notes: Sarbani is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is the embodiment of the grace and beauty of the earth, personified as the goddess Saraswati and Lakshmi. The name Sarbani carries the meaning “Goddess of the Earth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Bengali. Parents who choose Sarbani usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of the earth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the divine feminine energy, nurturing and creative, and the connection between the earth and the divine.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sarbani holds great significance in Indian culture, as it derives from the names of two revered Hindu goddesses, Saraswati and Lakshmi. Saraswati is the goddess of knowledge, music, art, wisdom, and learning, while Lakshmi is the goddess of prosperity, wealth, and good fortune. The name Sarbani not only reflects the divine blessings bestowed upon a child by these goddesses but also highlights the importance of education, art, and wealth in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Sarbani holds immense spiritual significance as it embodies the qualities of the goddesses Saraswati and Lakshmi. Saraswati represents knowledge, creativity, and wisdom, while Lakshmi abundant wealth and prosperity. The name Sarbani inspires individuals to strive towards spiritual growth, wisdom, and obtaining material wealth through honest means. It signifies the divine union of wisdom and prosperity in one's life, and the blessing of the two most powerful goddesses, Saraswati and Lakshmi.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sarbani: Radiant and Auspicious One, bearing the light of a thousand suns within.

historical_references.reference: Sarbani was a wife of King Shalivahana, also known as Salivahana or Satakarni, who ruled the Satavahana Kingdom during the 1st century AD. She is mentioned in the inscriptions found at Amaravati and Nandyal.

Sarbani is also the name of a goddess in the Hindu Puranic tradition, revered particularly in the eastern Indian states of Bengal and Odisha. Her origin myth involves her being born from the tears of Goddess Lakshmi when she wept over the suffering of the people in the age of Kali.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Sarbani, of Indian origin, has gained popularity in modern contexts across various platforms. Lastly, on LinkedIn, Sarbani is a common name among Indian professionals, where she is seen as a successful entrepreneur and business leader.
